agents.name: Pi

surface_source.quote: Beyond slash commands, Pi extensions can render custom TUI components directly in the terminal: spinners, progress bars, interactive file pickers, data tables, preview panes.

agents.quote: And Pi happens to be, at this point, the coding agent that I use almost exclusively.

surface_source.quote: Which basically means I run claude --dangerously-skip-permissions.

history.quote: I predominently use Claude Code with the cheaper Max subscription for $100 a month
At the moment I’m using Amp, Claude Code, and Pi, all from the command line.

agents.name: Codex
agents.quote: In the Codex harness I found multiple cases where subagents resorted fully to manual string manipulation with Python instead of using the patch tool.

history.quote: So I now use Codex on the command line to do reviews, but that means a whole part of my iteration cycles is invisible to other engineers on the team.

models.name: Sol
models.quote: Long story short: I had a conversation with Fable and Sol via Pi about what could be done with such a dongle or whether I should use a Raspberry Pi instead if I wanted to do my own thing there.

history.quote: I exclusively use the cheaper Sonnet model. It’s perfectly adequate for my needs, and in fact, I prefer its outputs over the more expensive Opus model.

review_style.value: Steers as it goes, reviews when the agent says done
review_style.quote: In the agent loop, the model eventually says “done” and I review. Even before that, I usually steer along the way.

also.quote: As more code is written by agents, it makes little sense to throw unfinished work at humans before an agent has reviewed it first.
It has shown that it will commit slop, and it requires me to review it more as a result.

harness.value: Pi in the terminal, forks in Ghostty splits, subagents in tmux
harness.quote:
`/split-fork` to branch the current session into a new Pi process in a right-hand Ghostty split.
Serial `subagent` tool that runs one observable Pi child at a time in tmux; attach with the printed `pi --attach-subagent …` command.

rules_files.value: AGENTS.md in his agent-stuff repo (12 lines)
rules_files.quote: Pi extensions live in `./extensions`. When working in this repo, add or update extensions there. You can consult the `pi-mono` for reference, but do not modify code in `pi-mono`.

mcp_servers.quote: There is no MCP, there are no community skills, nothing.

value: uv.ts: blocks pip and python, pushes the agent to uv
hooks.quote: Replaces the bash tool with a `uv`-aware version that injects Python command shims and blocks common non-`uv` workflows.

signature.caption: in place of plan mode
signature.why: Our pick: he skips plan mode and lets the agent ask questions in plain prose, then a self-built extension turns those questions into a form he fills in.
signature.quote: The problem: answering questions inline gets messy. So /answer reads the agent’s last response, extracts all the questions, and reformats them into a nice input box.

archetype.why: Has the agent write his own Pi extensions and 18 skills. No MCP, nothing downloaded.
